summary.intent: Resolve open PR review comments from automated reviewers by triaging, fixing, and replying to each unresolved thread.
summary.outcome: One of two unresolved threads was fixed (fetchShareKeys return type in share.service.ts dropping folder-ipns keys); the other was correctly identified as intentional behavior and marked not applicable. Fix was committed, pushed, and threads resolved.

repo: Write recipients are intentionally allowed to add folder-ipns keys (their own signing keys for subfolders they create) but NOT folder keys (only owner sets subfolder decryption keys) — this asymmetry is by design.
fetchShareKeys in apps/web/src/services/share.service.ts previously excluded folder-ipns from its return type and cast, silently dropping those keys.
The project uses pnpm with separate typecheck and lint steps; linting share.service.ts caught a follow-up issue after the initial edit.

code.finding: fetchShareKeys return type and internal cast omitted folder-ipns, causing those keys to be silently dropped; fixed by including folder-ipns in the type/cast.
Validation blocks folder key type for write recipients but intentionally allows folder-ipns — recipients self-wrap their own signing keys when creating subfolders.

workflow: Used GraphQL reviewThreads query to fetch unresolved PR threads, then REST to reply and GraphQL mutation to resolve — different APIs required for reply vs resolve.
Lint must be run after typecheck edits; a secondary lint error appeared after fixing the type issue and required a second edit pass.
Triage before fixing: one of two flagged comments was intentional behavior, not a bug — reading the code context before editing saved an incorrect change.

friction: A lint error surfaced after the initial fix edit, requiring a second read-edit-lint cycle on the same file.
CodeRabbit flagged intentional asymmetric permission logic as a bug, requiring careful reasoning about the design to avoid incorrectly 'fixing' it.
